sources_policy.authorship: All claim summaries below are original paraphrases. Source texts, dictionary paradigms and facsimiles are not copied into runtime data.
sources_policy.doom: Original Institute of Linguistics DOOM 3 website inspected in browser. Home explicitly identifies 2021 third edition (Univers Enciclopedic) and electronic CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. This establishes normative form facts, not synonym meaning; no unrestricted reuse permission inferred.
sources_policy.dlr: Academy/Institutul de Filologie Română Alexandru Philippide DA/DLR archive identifies its digital facsimiles as produced by the Institute within CLRE. Original scans visually read. Exact print volume/year collation incomplete; home dates DA 1913–1948 and DLR 1965–2010. No scan reproduction license verified; retain links and own paraphrases only.
sources_policy.press: Original Romanian publisher pages evidence their own word use, not every news fact. No prose/media imported; no blanket reuse license asserted.
sources_policy.digitizers: dexonline transcribes mixed dictionaries with attribution. Useful for counter-sense discovery; primary scans support conclusions. No uniform license/currentness/publisher-original status asserted.
sources_policy.limits: Attestations do not measure population familiarity, age-wide recognition, enjoyment, game difficulty or safe input ownership.

supported_claims.claim: Drapel is a lexical synonym of steag for the physical flag serving as a group/state/institution emblem.
Normative headword and directly listed plural are drapel and drapele.
Official Romanian usage is current, and the historical dictionary contains older literary/institutional attestations.

leads.counter_senses_and_register: DLR has separate fabric, pavilion, aviation blade-position and foundry usages; military/figurative expressions are not a license to collapse all senses. DOOM displays no register restriction on the headword. The main emblem sense is not limited to military flags. Cinema-lighting sense was found only in attributed MDN transcription.
held_claims: Whole-word equivalence across every specialist/figurative sense.
Any aliases beyond exactly researched headword; complete inflection family not inferred.
Compatibility with the existing Steag incident edges, player inputs, historical records and all consumers; root/review responsibility.
leads.next_action: Compare exact existing Steag sense and consumer contexts against physical emblem sense before any bounded input proposal.

supported_claims.claim: In the employee-pay sense, leafă denotes periodic remuneration and is explicitly linked to salariu.
DOOM payment entry lists leafă, articulated genitive/dative lefii and plural lefuri; the distinct regional utensil entry has plural lefi.
Published Romanian use spans 2008 and 2024 with leafă referring to salary.

leads.counter_senses_and_register: DOOM marks the utensil/găvan homonym regional, not the remuneration entry. Do not describe all leafă use as archaic. DLR separately marks historical military pay old, and its broader service-pay definition can include payment in produce. No blanket identity with income, honorarium, every wage arrangement or all historical military senses. DLR and DOOM homonym numbering differs: DLR leafă¹ sense 2 is pay; DOOM leafă² is pay.
held_claims: Prior i05 hold is not lifted by source access alone; dominant game sense and consumer/history clearance remain unresolved.
No lefi salary plural added from historical entries; DOOM payment plural is lefuri.
No blanket synonym equivalence with every remuneration or income concept.
leads.next_action: Attach this new primary evidence to the existing held record, then independently reassess exact salary-owner contexts and ambiguity.

supported_claims.claim: The ordinary travel-container sense of valiză explicitly includes geamantan in primary DLR.
Normative headword and directly listed plural are geamantan and geamantane.
A 2024 original Romanian interview uses geamantan for travel luggage.

leads.counter_senses_and_register: DLR valiză¹ also includes large luggage bags and a diplomatic compound covering bags/packages, while valiză² is a regional timber-channel homonym. Older DN/MDN transcriptions qualify valiză as a small geamantan; do not universalize that size restriction or alias every geantă/bagaj/cufăr. DOOM geamantan has no displayed restriction label.
